requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) serves DHCP from its own pool on lan-a, handing node3 an address plus itself as default gateway (not static config on node3)
requirements.summary: VyOS eth2 set to 10.10.1.1/24; Kea DHCP4 shared-network LANA subnet 10.10.1.0/24 with range 10.10.1.100-200 and default-router 10.10.1.1 committed and saved (cmd-eb5ebb0337bb4398). kea-dhcp4 confirmed running on eth2 (cmd-197fb53df6a64011). node3's second NIC was converted from a manual test-IP/no-config state to a NetworkManager DHCP-client profile (ipv4.method=auto), which obtained 10.10.1.100/24 with default route via 10.10.1.1 (cmd-3c687ed9ed0144d8). node1's lease file independently records node3's assignment (cmd-cd72fc2352f647ac).

requirements.requirement: node2 (OPNsense) serves DHCP from its own pool on lan-b, handing node4 an address plus itself as default gateway (not static config on node4)
requirements.summary: OPNsense opt1/vtnet2 configured with static 10.10.2.1/24 and Kea DHCPv4 subnet4 10.10.2.0/24, pool 10.10.2.100-200, router 10.10.2.1 (cmd-c749dd3793d448c1, cmd-b0bc1a21e2b94465). A pre-existing baseline dnsmasq service was found wildcard-bound to UDP/67 blocking Kea; root-caused via Kea logs and pf/dnsmasq inspection and resolved by disabling dnsmasq (cmd-e74484d758b74a43, cmd-01ac2373bb834153, cmd-2b15c0ff805c43d3), after which kea-dhcp4 bound cleanly to 10.10.2.1:67 (cmd-f6e2d59236164d0f). node4's NIC was moved to a NetworkManager DHCP-client profile and obtained 10.10.2.100/24 with default route via 10.10.2.1 (cmd-72788aba1e044392); node2's lease file confirms node4's assignment (cmd-f0cd2b8ffedd46f4).

requirements.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/gateway state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id e636d872... with eth2 configured and kea-dhcp4 running captured pre-restart (cmd-581c7097ef98478b). Reboot command issued and acknowledged (cmd-5e6349465f5e4c5d), connection interruption observed, and a new boot_id 3488a1db... confirmed post-restart (cmd-c041a6745b0645f2). eth2 address, kea process, and lease file all confirmed intact after restart (cmd-7a4b28cfdbf944d7), and node3's ping to the gateway succeeded post-restart (cmd-864f5b3410e74c9c), consistent with the independent lifecycle snapshot showing a differing boot-identity between before-prepare and after-executor.

requirements.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/gateway state
requirements.summary: Baseline kern.boottime 05:08:17 with vtnet2/Kea healthy captured pre-restart (cmd-d232b99044804c7b). Reboot acknowledged (cmd-a6730b7689644d05), SSH transport dropped as expected, and a new kern.boottime 05:27:36 confirmed post-restart (cmd-43c8a895234f463d). vtnet2 address, kea bound to 10.10.2.1:67, and the lease file all confirmed intact (cmd-135c9ffd455b4128), and node4's ping to the gateway succeeded post-restart (cmd-cb775d3e82824e92).

requirements.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, and recovered DHCP-obtained addressing/route
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id b17495e3... with enp8s0 leased and gateway reachable captured pre-restart (cmd-1818d274335b4b38). Reboot acknowledged with a connection reset confirming shutdown (cmd-c49e4b32c6a244e5), and a new boot_id 7295357f... confirmed post-restart (cmd-451d3e83878045b0). enp8s0's DHCP lease/default route were automatically reacquired via NetworkManager and gateway ping succeeded (cmd-c98aa10935ba4526).

requirements.requirement: node4 restart: healthy baseline, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, and recovered DHCP-obtained addressing/route
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 19062a82... with enp8s0 leased and gateway reachable captured pre-restart (cmd-6f74069d29014e57). Reboot acknowledged with a connection timeout confirming shutdown (cmd-d1d75355ade64fe4), and a new boot_id 1ef6907f... confirmed post-restart (cmd-571811eee17741df). enp8s0's DHCP lease/default route were automatically reacquired and gateway ping succeeded (cmd-e249f57ac2644701).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were satisfied with direct evidence: node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) each serve DHCP from their own lan-a/lan-b pools handing out themselves as default gateway, and node3/node4 were converted from static/unconfigured NICs to NetworkManager DHCP clients that successfully obtained addressing and default routes from their respective routers, confirmed by lease files on both routers and successful pings. The OPNsense side required legitimate troubleshooting (a UDP/67 bind conflict with a pre-existing dnsmasq service) that was correctly root-caused and resolved. The independently-required node-restart evidence protocol was completed for all four nodes with pre-restart healthy baselines, acknowledged restarts, distinct post-restart boot identities, and confirmed recovery of DHCP service/lease state and gateway connectivity, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: The pf firewall pass-all rule added directly to OPNsense's config.xml for lan-b ('antrieb: allow LANB to any') was not evaluated for scope/security tightness beyond confirming it enables connectivity; it may be broader than strictly necessary.

It could not be independently confirmed from the trace whether the abandoned legacy <dhcpd><opt1> XML block on node2 was removed or left in config.xml, since no explicit cleanup command was observed after the switch to the Kea-based approach.

VyOS DHCP lease and default-router verification relied on the node3/node4 client-side route table and the server-side lease CSV; no independent packet capture of DHCP OFFER/ACK options was available to directly show the 'default-router' option value in transit.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing actions were tightly scoped to diagnosis or the final solution. Temporary test IPs added on node1 (eth1/eth2, cmd-1c732c98dcda44db), node2 (vtnet1/vtnet2, cmd-a2498ff6feba416a), node3 (enp8s0, cmd-a0f4024d5eaf4ed2), and node4 (enp8s0, cmd-ccc833396a754eca) for arping-based topology discovery were bounded, low-risk, and fully reverted shortly afterward (cmd-5cc1ca97222c4039, cmd-052b0a9623174841, cmd-dd032c55d3214c45, cmd-1b8e5db0166543f8). Disabling the pre-existing baseline dnsmasq service on node2 (cmd-2b15c0ff805c43d3) was a necessary, well-diagnosed prerequisite to free UDP/67 for Kea and is retained, which is appropriate since dnsmasq was not part of the task's required lan-b DHCP path. One residual item was not cleaned up: an initial attempt to configure lan-b DHCP via OPNsense's legacy ISC 'dhcpd' XML model (cmd-261fc72bf2d646a9, adding an opt1 stanza under <dhcpd>) was abandoned in favor of the Kea-based approach actually used, but the leftover dhcpd/opt1 config block does not appear to have been removed from config.xml, leaving small unused residue (a service that is never enabled, so it has no functional impact). Config.xml backup files (.bak-lanb, .bak-kea, .bak-dnsmasq) were created before edits as a reasonable safety practice and are harmless residue. Two commands hit a 120s proxy timeout during dnsmasq/kea service restarts (cmd-d7725fb276d449ea, cmd-112f35c0ab5149d8) but follow-up checks confirmed the intended state was reached, so these are not treated as failures.
